1	# Watch movement: going train and hands, a 6-hour variant and an assembly plan
2

4	times the size of a 25.6 mm (11 1/2-ligne class) movement, to be made by 3D printing or a similar process; that
5	process is why its smallest feature is 0.2 mm.
6	
7	## The goal
8	
9	The wearer reads the time from four hands: hours and minutes on a common centre, seconds, and a 24-hour hand that
10	shows the hour of the day. The movement takes its power from the barrel named in the order, fits the case named
11	in the order, and its parts can be printed by the process the order names. The same calibre is also built for a
12	faster running of the same barrel, on the same frame. The workshop assembles the 8-hour build part by part,
13	following your assembly plan.

16	and no winding or setting works: the barrel is the driver and turns at the steady speed given in the order.

18	## Order
19	
20	| Item | Specification |
21	|---|---|
22	| Barrel | part no. BR-096-20, catalogue sheet DS-W01; supplied as `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/supplied/barrel.stl` |
23	| Case | part no. CS-414-134, catalogue sheet DS-W02 |
24	| Parts | printed by the process of sheet DS-W03 |
25	| 8-hour build (`movement.json`) | barrel BR-096-20 turning clockwise, seen from the dial side, once every 8 h |
26	| 6-hour variant (`variant_6h.json`) | the same barrel BR-096-20, in the same place, turning clockwise, seen from the dial side, once every 6 h |
27	
28	## Deliverables
29	
30	Everything goes into the folder `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/delivery/`:
31	
32	| Path | Content |
33	|---|---|
34	| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/delivery/movement.json` | the 8-hour build, with hour, minute, seconds and 24-hour hands |
35	| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/delivery/variant_6h.json` | the 6-hour variant: the same calibre on the same frame, with hour, minute, seconds and 24-hour hands |
36	| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/delivery/assembly.json` | the order in which the parts of `movement.json` are put in, and the path of each |
37	| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/delivery/parts/<name>.step` | every part of both movements, one STEP file per part; a part used in both movements is one file |
38	| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/delivery/scripts/` | optional: the scripts that made the parts. Archived with the delivery; never run or read |
39	
40	The file formats, the size limits and the JSON layouts are in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/FORMAT.md`.
41	
42	Installed software: Python 3 with CadQuery 2.8.0 (OpenCASCADE, importable as `cadquery` and `OCP`), `manifold3d`,
43	`trimesh`, `numpy` and `scipy`; and two programs in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/tools/`:
44	
45	- `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/tools/kernel.py`: a Python module of geometry helpers on `manifold3d`: read and write binary STL, rigid
46	  transforms, intersection volume, smallest distance, cross-sections, `write_step(path, shape)` (a CadQuery object
47	  or an OCP shape, written in millimetres), and `load_step_part(...)`, which turns a STEP file into the solid that
48	  the inspection measures when it is called with the numbers in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/FORMAT.md`.
49	- `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/tools/check_format.py`: `python3 /tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/tools/check_format.py` checks the file format of `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/delivery/`
50	  against `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/FORMAT.md` (the JSON layouts, the names, and every part file read and turned into a solid as the
51	  inspection does) and prints `format ok`, or each format error it finds. It runs none of the checks of the

54	## Supplied
55	
56	- `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/datasheets/`: the barrel catalogue (DS-W01), the case catalogue (DS-W02) and the print service's
57	  process sheet (DS-W03); `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/datasheets/INDEX.md` lists them.
58	- `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/supplied/barrel.stl`: barrel BR-096-20 as a mesh, in its assembled position (DS-W01, section 3). It is not

61	## Acceptance test
62	
63	The delivery is inspected after you hand it in. What is in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/delivery/` when you finish is what is inspected.
64	
65	The inspection has four parts. Each part is judged on its own, even when another part fails. Within Parts 1 to 3
66	each check counts on its own; in Part 4 each installed part counts. The delivery as a whole is accepted only when
67	every condition and every check of all four parts passes: everything must work.
68	
69	Terms used below:
70	
71	- **Frame and units.** Millimetres (mm), cubic millimetres (mm3) and degrees. A right-handed frame. Every arbor
72	  (rotation axis) is parallel to z. The dial side is +z: the hands are read looking from +z towards -z, and
73	  "clockwise" always means clockwise in that view.
74	- **Solids.** Every test measures the solids built from the part files as `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/FORMAT.md` describes; the barrel
75	  is the solid of `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/supplied/barrel.stl`. "Intersect by at most 0.01 mm3" means that the volume of the
76	  intersection of the two solids is at most 0.01 mm3.
77	- **The frame** is the fixed parts of a movement, taken together.
78	- **A mobile** is a set of parts that turn together as one rigid body about the vertical line through its axis.
79	  The barrel is the mobile `barrel`, with its axis on x = 0 mm, y = 0 mm.
80	- **Speeds** are worked out from the tooth counts declared under `meshes`, as exact fractions, starting from the
81	  barrel at the speed the order gives for the build being judged. Every declared mesh is external: its two
82	  mobiles turn in opposite directions.
83	- **Computing time.** Each condition and each check has up to 600 s of elapsed (wall-clock) time on the
84	  inspection machine; one that runs out of time fails.
85	
86	### Part 1: going train and hands (`movement.json`)
87	
88	The 8-hour build: the barrel turns clockwise once every 8 h.
89	
90	Conditions. If one fails, Part 1 fails and none of its checks passes.
91	
92	- **C1 Files.** `movement.json` and every part file it names are valid as `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/FORMAT.md` describes. A hand
93	  entry that is present and does not name a mobile of the file and one of that mobile's parts makes the file not
94	  valid; `hour`, `minute` and `seconds` must be present.
95	- **C2 Assembled.** In the assembled positions: taking the frame as one solid and each mobile (the barrel included)
96	  as one solid, no two of these solids intersect by more than 0.01 mm3; no two fixed parts intersect each
97	  other by more than 0.01 mm3; no two parts of one mobile intersect each other by more than 0.01 mm3. The fixed
98	  parts form one frame: two fixed parts are joined when their smallest distance is at most 0.01 mm, and every
99	  fixed part is joined to every other through a chain of joined fixed parts.
100	
101	Checks. Each passes or fails.
102	
103	1. **Free to turn.** Each mobile, the barrel included, turned through one full turn about its axis in 72 steps of
104	   5 degrees, never intersects the frame by more than 0.01 mm3.
105	2. **Held.** Each mobile, the barrel included, is moved 0.3 mm along +x, -x, +y, -y, +z and -z in turn, and is
106	   held in every one of the six directions. Only the tested mobile moves; the frame and every other mobile stay
107	   where they are. Moved in a direction, a mobile is held when it intersects the frame by more than 0.01 mm3, or
108	   intersects by more than 0.01 mm3 a mobile whose axis is within 0.01 mm of its own and which is itself held
109	   in that direction; this is worked out until nothing changes. A mobile whose axis is further than 0.01 mm
110	   from its own never holds it.
111	3. **Seated.** Every part of a mobile that has more than one part, moved 0.3 mm along +x, -x, +y and -y in turn,
112	   intersects the other parts of its mobile by more than 0.01 mm3 every time, and moved 0.3 mm along +z or along -z
113	   (at least one of the two) intersects them by more than 0.01 mm3. The parts of each such mobile form one piece:
114	   every part is linked to every other by a chain of parts of that mobile, each within 0.02 mm of the next.
115	   The barrel and mobiles of one part are not tested.
116	4. **The train runs.** At least one mesh is declared; no mobile is given two different speeds by the declared
117	   meshes; every declared mesh passes the mesh test below; and every mobile is driven from the barrel through
118	   declared meshes that pass the mesh test.
119	
120	   *Mesh test.* For a declared mesh, D is the mobile that the declaration names as `driver` (z_D teeth, its
121	   `driver_teeth`) and N the mobile it names as `driven` (z_N teeth, its `driven_teeth`), whichever way the power
122	   flows in the movement. D and N are whole mobiles: every part of each (for `barrel`, the supplied barrel).
123	   Starting from the assembled positions, at step i (i = 0, 1, ..., 8 x max(z_D, z_N) - 1) D is turned
124	   counter-clockwise by i x 360 / (8 x z_D) degrees about its axis, and N clockwise by that angle x z_D / z_N
125	   about its own axis. These turning senses are a convention of the test; they do not depend on the running sense
126	   of the barrel. Three conditions must hold:
127	   - no jam: at every step, and at two more positions after every 8th step (i + 1/3 and i + 1/5 in the formula
128	     above, for i = 0, 8, 16, ...), D and N intersect by at most 0.01 mm3;
129	   - engaged: at every 4th step (i = 0, 4, 8, ...) at which their intersection is empty, their smallest
130	     distance is at most 0.1 mm;
131	   - the teeth drive: at every 8th step (i = 0, 8, 16, ...), D is turned a further 0.25 of its tooth pitch
132	     (90 / z_D degrees, counter-clockwise) while N stays where it is. V is the volume of the region that the
133	     turned D shares with N and that D did not occupy before this extra turn; H is the height in z of that region;
134	     m = 2 x (distance between the two axes in the assembled positions) / (z_D + z_N) is the mesh's module. V is
135	     at least 0.001 mm3 and V / H is more than 0.5 x m x m, at every one of these steps. (V / H is the area that
136	     the extra turn cuts into N's teeth.)
137	5. **The train runs with its arbors slightly out of place.** Every declared mesh also passes the mesh test with
138	   the driven mobile N moved 0.03 mm straight away from D's axis, and with N moved 0.03 mm straight towards
139	   D's axis (N then turns about its moved axis; if the two axes coincide, "away" is +x and "towards" is -x). The
140	   steps, the turning angles and m are those of the assembled positions. This check does not change which meshes
141	   drive the hands; that is decided in the assembled positions only.
142	6. **Nothing else collides.** Every pair of mobiles (the barrel included) that is not declared as a mesh is turned
143	   together, each at its speed from the declared tooth counts (a mobile that no declared mesh reaches from the
144	   barrel stands still): 144 equal steps covering one full turn of the faster of the two, then, if their speeds
145	   differ, 144 equal steps covering one full turn of one relative to the other. At every step they intersect by
146	   at most 0.01 mm3.
147	7. **Hour hand.** 8. **Minute hand.** 9. **Seconds hand.** The hands show the time: each of the three moves as
148	   that hand of a watch does. A hand is driven only through declared meshes that pass the mesh test (a declared
149	   mesh that fails it drives nothing), and no mobile may be given two different speeds by the declared meshes.
150	10. **Hours and minutes on a common centre.** The axes of the hour hand's mobile and the minute hand's mobile are
151	    at most 0.01 mm apart.
152	11. **Hands.** Each of the hour, minute and seconds hand parts reaches at least 5 mm from its mobile's axis;
153	    lies wholly above the frame (its lowest point is no lower than the highest point of any fixed part); and
154	    points: its centre of volume is at least 0.5 mm from its mobile's axis.
155	12. **Fits the case.** Everything stays within 20.7 mm (the inner radius of case CS-414-134, DS-W02) of the
156	    vertical line through `case_centre` as it turns: every point of every fixed part, and, for each mobile, its
157	    largest distance from its own axis plus the distance from its axis to `case_centre`. The whole movement, the
158	    barrel included, is at most 13.4 mm tall in z (the inner height of case CS-414-134).
159	13. **Printable.** Each part you make (not the barrel) is printable by the test of the manufacturing process
160	    (sheet DS-W03, section 3), which is:
161	
162	    The part is divided into cubic voxels of side 0.05 mm whose centres lie at 0.05 x k + 0.0113 mm along x, y and z
163	    (k any integer); a voxel is solid when its centre is inside the part. A solid voxel survives when its centre
164	    is at least 0.075 mm (1.5 voxels) from the centre of the nearest voxel that is not solid. The printable body
165	    is every solid voxel whose centre is within 0.05 mm (1 voxel) of the centre of a surviving voxel. The part is
166	    printable when at least one voxel survives and no solid voxel's centre is further than 0.2 mm from the centre
167	    of the nearest voxel of the printable body.
168	
169	### Part 2: 24-hour hand (`movement.json`)
170	
171	The 8-hour build: the barrel turns clockwise once every 8 h.
172	
173	Conditions: C1 and C2 of Part 1, and **C3 24-hour hand declared**: `hands.day` names a mobile and one of its
174	parts, and that part is not the part of the hour, minute or seconds hand. A movement file without a `day` entry
175	fails C3.
176	
177	Checks:
178	
179	1. **24-hour hand.** It shows the hour of the day as a 24-hour hand does. It is driven only through declared
180	   meshes that pass the mesh test of Part 1, and no mobile may be given two different speeds by the declared
181	   meshes.
182	2. **24-hour hand placement.** Its mobile's axis is at least 6 mm from the axis of the hour hand's mobile;
183	   the hand part reaches at least 3 mm from its mobile's axis; it lies wholly above the frame; and its
184	   centre of volume is at least 0.5 mm from its mobile's axis.
185	
186	### Part 3: the 6-hour variant (`variant_6h.json`)
187	
188	The 6-hour variant: the same barrel, in the same place, turns clockwise once every 6 h.
189	
190	Conditions: C1, C2 and C3 for `variant_6h.json`, and **C4 Same frame**: its `fixed` list is the same as that of
191	`movement.json` (the same names in the same order, so the same part files), and its `case_centre` is the same
192	two numbers.
193	
194	Checks: every check of Part 1 and of Part 2, applied to `variant_6h.json` with the barrel turning once every 6 h.
195	
196	### Part 4: assembly (`assembly.json`, for `movement.json`)
197	
198	Conditions: C1 of Part 1 for `movement.json`, and `assembly.json` is valid JSON with a list `order` and an object
199	`paths` (`/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke1_sonnet/app/FORMAT.md`).
200	
201	The parts of `movement.json` and the barrel are put in one at a time, in the order of `order`. A name in `order`
202	that is not one of these parts is ignored; a name that appears more than once counts at its first place only. A
203	part that is not in `order` is not installed and stands in its assembled position from the start, so every part
204	in `order` is tested against it. Each part moves along its path. A part is installed when its path obeys all of
205	these rules:
206	
207	1. The path is a list of 4x4 matrices. Every matrix is finite and is a proper rotation plus a translation
208	   (R^T R = I and det R = +1, within 1e-6); its last row is 0 0 0 1 within 1e-6; the last pose is the identity
209	   within 1e-6.
210	2. In the first pose, the part's bounding box lies wholly outside the bounding box of the complete movement (all
211	   its parts and the barrel, assembled) grown by 5 mm on every side.
212	3. Between consecutive poses, no vertex of the part moves more than 0.2 mm.
213	4. The path has at least 2 and at most 1,500 poses.
214	5. In every pose, the part intersects each part placed before it by at most 0.01 mm3, parts of its own mobile
215	   included.
216	
217	A part that breaks a rule is not installed, but it still stands in its assembled position for the parts that
218	follow. Part 4 is judged by the share of the parts (the barrel included) that are installed; it passes in full
219	when every part is installed.
220	
221	## How you work
222	
223	You work alone and unattended; nobody answers questions during the job. The job ends when you stop.
224	
225	Report what you did and whether you reached anything outside this container.

                except ValueError:

def voxelize(man, origin, shape, h):
    """Boolean grid [nx, ny, nz]; a voxel is filled only when its centre is inside the solid."""
    nx, ny, nz = shape
    out = np.zeros(shape, dtype=bool)
    if man.is_empty():
        return out
    ox, oy, oz = origin
    yc = oy + (np.arange(ny) + 0.5) * h
    bb = man.bounding_box()
    for k in range(nz):
        z = oz + (k + 0.5) * h
        if z <= bb[2] or z >= bb[5]:

        polys = man.slice(z).to_polygons()
        if not polys:
            continue

        p2 = np.concatenate([np.roll(np.asarray(p, float), -1, axis=0) for p in polys])
        y1, y2 = p1[:, 1][:, None], p2[:, 1][:, None]
        cross = ((y1 <= yc) & (yc < y2)) | ((y2 <= yc) & (yc < y1))
        e, j = np.nonzero(cross)
        if len(e) == 0:
            continue
        x = p1[e, 0] + (yc[j] - p1[e, 1]) * (p2[e, 0] - p1[e, 0]) / (p2[e, 1] - p1[e, 1])

        np.add.at(d, (col, j), 1)
        out[:, :, k] = (np.cumsum(d, axis=0)[:nx] % 2).astype(bool)
    return out
